context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using Google Cloud Platform.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU and US)
- Licensed Clinicians
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (GCP hosted in europe-west3 and us-central1)
- External Pharmacies (EU national e-prescription networks and US pharmacy systems)
- Regional Payment Gateways (Stripe/regional processors)
- Health Authorities & Auditors (FDA, EMA, national ministries)
- Identity Providers (eIDAS for EU, OAuth2/OIDC for US)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform via HTTPS and WebRTC (SRTP/DTLS-SRTP)
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> External Pharmacies via REST and HL7 FHIR
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> Regional Payment Gateways via HTTPS REST API
- Health Authorities & Auditors -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform via zero-trust read-only audit proxies over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for data residency compliance
- WebRTC / SRTP: For video consultations with low-bandwidth adaptation (<300 kbit/s)
- HL7 FHIR & REST: For US pharmacy interoperability and external integrations
- WORM Storage: For immutable regional AI symptom-checker audit logging (R-07)
- OAuth2 / OIDC / eIDAS: For federated authentication and consent-driven access control (R-04)
- GCP Cloud CDN: For global edge caching of static client assets

## Rationale
This architecture isolates data regionally in GCP to strictly satisfy GDPR and HIPAA mandates while supporting cross-border care. It ensures high availability and accountability for rural users and regulated medical AI tools through robust edge routing and immutable regional logging.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. Core purpose is delivering secure, compliant telemedicine services across international jurisdictions with strict data residency.]

## Key Elements
*   Patients (EU and US)
*   Licensed Clinicians
*   Platform Administrators / Compliance Officers
*   Web App & Mobile App (React / Flutter)
*   API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Envoy)
*   Identity & Access Management (IAM) / Consent Service
*   Core Services Container (Spring Boot / Java)
*   AI Symptom Checker Container (Python / FastAPI / PyTorch with MLflow)
*   SFU Video Container (LiveKit / Janus)
*   Async Event Broker (Google Cloud Pub/Sub)
*   Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage)
*   External Pharmacies, Regional Payment Gateways, Health Authorities & Auditors, Identity Providers

## Relationships
*   Patients / Clinicians to Web App & Mobile App via HTTPS/JSON and WebRTC (Video)
*   Web App / Mobile App to API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
*   API Gateway to Core Services, AI Symptom Checker, and Consent Service via gRPC with mTLS (Istio/Anthos)
*   Core Services to Async Event Broker via AMQP/Pub/Sub protocols
*   Core Services to Data Storage via secure database connections with CMEK encryption
*   Async Event Broker to External Pharmacies via encrypted HTTPS

## Technology Stack
*   Cloud Provider: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for regional data isolation
*   Orchestration & Mesh: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) with Istio/Anthos service mesh for zero-trust mTLS
*   Backend Services: Spring Boot (Java) for core logic; Python (FastAPI/PyTorch) with MLflow for AI traceability
*   Frontend: React and Flutter for cross-platform support with degraded video handling (<300 kbit/s)
*   Real-Time & Messaging: LiveKit or Janus SFU for video; Google Cloud Pub/Sub with Dead Letter Queues for async events
*   Security & Compliance: Cloud KMS with CMEK, Google Secret Manager, and OpenTelemetry for immutable audit logs

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces strict regional data residency on GCP to comply with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR mandates. Resilient video streaming and async messaging ensure high availability for rural users and unstable connections.]

Web App & Mobile App.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability for rural users.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU and US) and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
- Web App & Mobile App Container (React / Flutter)
- Consent & Routing Controller Component
- Resilient Video Client Component (WebRTC)
- Offline-First Symptom Module Component (SQLCipher/IndexedDB)
- API & SFU Client Component
- Localization & a11y Provider Component
- API Gateway and SFU Video Container

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Web App & Mobile App: HTTPS/JSON and WebRTC (Video)
- Web App & Mobile App -> API Gateway: HTTPS/TLS 1.3 with regional routing headers, app version hashes, and encrypted payloads
- Resilient Video Client -> SFU Video Container: WebRTC signaling and media streaming with adaptive bitrate

## Technology Stack
- React (Web) and Flutter (Mobile): Cross-platform UI development
- SQLCipher / IndexedDB: Client-side encrypted local caching for offline-first symptom checking
- WebRTC & LiveKit/Janus: Real-time video consultations supporting degraded network modes (<300 kbit/s)
- Sentry / OpenTelemetry: Client-side RUM, error tracking, and performance monitoring
- OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Secure session management and token handling

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict regional data compliance and resilience for unstable rural internet connections. Client-side encryption, robust telemetry, and modular components support EU MDR traceability and HIPAA security standards.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency and compliance via dedicated, stateless regional API gateways.

## Key Elements
* Patients (EU and US) and Licensed Clinicians
* External Pharmacies and Regional Payment Gateways
* `EU API Gateway` (Envoy / GCP Cloud Endpoints in `europe-west3`)
* `US API Gateway` (Envoy / GCP Cloud Endpoints in `us-central1`)
* Regional Memorystore (Redis) for Idempotency
* IAM & Consent Service
* Core Services Container and AI Symptom Checker Container
* Istio Service Mesh

## Relationships
* Web & Mobile App -> API Gateway: Sends API requests and mutations over [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
* API Gateway -> Regional Memorystore: Checks request deduplication via [Redis Protocol / TLS with connection pooling]
* API Gateway -> Core Services / AI Symptom Checker / IAM: Routes valid requests via [gRPC with mTLS via Istio]
* API Gateway -> Audit Sinks: Exports compliance and consent telemetry asynchronously

## Technology Stack
* Envoy / GCP Cloud Endpoints: Perimeter routing, TLS 1.3 termination, rate limiting, and circuit breaking
* GCP Cloud Memorystore (Redis): Regional idempotency cache preserving stateless gateway design
* Istio Service Mesh: Internal mTLS communication, canary deployments, and traffic shedding
* OAuth2 / OIDC: Token-based authentication embedding consent scopes for local gateway validation
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing and structured access logging routed to region-locked audit sinks

## Rationale
Decomposing the API Gateway into region-specific, stateless instances guarantees that health data residency is strictly enforced within `europe-west3` and `us-central1` per GDPR and HIPAA. Incorporating local JWT consent validation, rate limiting, and Redis idempotency protects rural mobile users from retry storms while maintaining high availability and security.

## Overview
[The Identity & Access Management (IAM) and Consent Service manages user authentication, authorization, and granular consent-driven access for the Cross-Border Telehealth Platform. It enforces regional data residency and regulatory compliance across EU and US deployments.]

## Key Elements
• Authentication Component (Spring Security / OIDC)
• Consent Engine (Spring Boot / Domain Model)

• Policy Enforcement Interceptor (gRPC / Envoy Filter)
• Revocation Cache Component (Google Cloud Memorystore Redis)
• External Identity Providers (eIDAS, OAuth2/OIDC IdPs)
• Google Secret Manager

• API Gateway -> Policy Enforcement Interceptor: Validates requests [gRPC with mTLS via Istio/Anthos]

• Consent Engine -> Consent Ledger: Persists immutable logs [PostgreSQL with CMEK]

## Technology Stack
• Spring Boot / Java: Core framework for IAM and Consent Engine services due to enterprise maturity
• Google Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Regional database instances chosen to enforce strict data residency (R-05)
• Google Cloud Memorystore (Redis): Regional caching for low-latency revocation checks without cross-region leaks
• Google Secret Manager: Manages secure credentials and OIDC client secrets with automated rotation

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces strict regional data residency and regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA) through isolated GCP deployments in Europe and the US. The combination of short-lived JWTs, regional Redis caching, and a gRPC policy interceptor ensures low-latency validation while protecting patient data.]

Core Services Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture uses a multi-region Google Cloud Platform deployment to enforce strict regional data residency and compliance.

## Key Elements
* Patients (EU and US) and Licensed Clinicians
* API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Envoy)
* Core Services Container (Spring Boot / Java) with internal components: Patient Management & Consent, E-Prescription Routing, Clinical Documentation, and Interoperability & Translation
* Identity & Access Management / Consent Service (OAuth2 / OIDC)
* Async Event Broker (Google Cloud Pub/Sub with DLQ)
* Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL with CMEK)
* External Pharmacies and Regional Payment Gateways

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Core Services Container: Routes validated requests via gRPC with mTLS
* Patient Management & Consent Component -> Data Storage: Reads and writes encrypted relational data using CMEK
* E-Prescription Routing Component -> Async Event Broker: Publishes asynchronous prescription events via AMQP/Pub/Sub
* Interoperability & Translation Component -> External Pharmacies: Transmits prescriptions via outbound HTTPS REST/SOAP with mTLS and circuit breaking

## Technology Stack
* Spring Boot / Java: Core business logic container for performance and enterprise ecosystem
* Google Cloud Platform (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data separation constraints
* Google Cloud Pub/Sub: Manages reliable asynchronous messaging and dead-letter queues for degraded network resilience
* PostgreSQL with CMEK: Provides encrypted, region-locked relational data storage
* OpenTelemetry & Istio: Enables distributed tracing and mTLS service mesh security

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating regional data while permitting cross-border care through verified patient consent. Additionally, it ensures high availability and accountability for rural users via asynchronous queuing and immutable audit logging.

Cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. Ensures GDPR and HIPAA compliance with strict regional data residency.

- Kubernetes / Istio: Regional deployments, canary rollouts, and traffic management.

Regional container isolation in GCP guarantees strict compliance with EU GDPR and US HIPAA mandates. Decoupled async auditing and strict input validation ensure EU MDR traceability, security, and high availability for rural users.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The system enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using GCP services.

- W3C Trace Context: Mandates distributed tracing across async boundaries for traceability.

## Rationale
The architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating EU and US health data regionally using GCP services and CMEK encryption. Asynchronous event brokering with robust DLQ management guarantees service availability and traceability for patients with unstable internet connections.
